name: OD600 to Cell Density Calculator
seoTitle: OD600 to Cell Density Calculator — Formula & Results
seoDesc: OD600 is the fastest way to follow a bacterial culture, but it is an optical reading, not a cell count. Free od600 to cell density calculator: enter your valu
summary:
OD600 is the fastest way to follow a bacterial culture, but it is an optical reading, not a cell count. It returns corrected OD600, cell density and dry cell weight, and the panel shows all of them at once.

This calculator converts absorbance to cells/mL and to dry cell weight using the standard factors, with a dilution correction for readings above 1. Press Calculate and the results appear in the grey boxes; after the first press they keep up with every edit, so there is no page to reload. Units are stated on every box and in every result, so a figure copied out of a protocol, a datasheet or a chart can be entered without converting it first.

sections.title: The formula behind the OD600 to Cell Density
sections.html:
Cells/mL = OD600 × dilution × (cells/mL per OD unit)

The symbols in the formula
SymbolWhat it stands forUnit
OD600absorbance at 600 nm against a medium blankAU
dilutionhow much the sample was diluted before reading×
factorstrain-specific conversioncells/mL per OD

sections.title: How do I use the OD600 to Cell Density?
sections.html:
Every input sits in the same order the formula is written, so the page reads like the equation.

  1. Enter the values you already have. Every box accepts a decimal point and a minus sign; thousands separators are ignored.
  2. The grey boxes are results: they are worked out from your inputs and cannot be typed into.
  3. Press Calculate. The results fill in together, and from then on they follow every edit you make — there is no page to reload and nothing to submit.

sections.title: A worked example
sections.html:
Take the default values the page opens with: od600 reading of 0.45, dilution before reading of 1 ×, cells/ml per od unit of 800,000,000 cells/mL, dry cell weight per od unit of 0.4 g/L.

Substituting them into the formula gives corrected od600 of 0.45, cell density of 360,000,000 cells/mL, dry cell weight of 0.18 g/L.

Those numbers come from the same solver the page runs in your browser, not from an illustration, so typing different inputs moves the answer exactly as the arithmetic says.

sections.title: What does the result mean?
sections.html:
The number on its own is not a judgement. These are the bands most often used when the result is quoted in a paper, a report or a label:

How to read the result
ResultBandWhat it means
0.1 – 1.0Linearthe reliable range of the spectrophotometer
1.0 – 1.5Edgedilute to be safe
above 1.5Non-linearalways dilute and correct

  • The factor depends on the strain, the medium and the instrument (path length). Calibrate it once against a haemocytometer count or a plate count for your own system.

  • The relationship is only linear up to about 1.0; above that, dilution is mandatory rather than optional.

  • OD600 counts dead cells as well as live ones, so it is a biomass measure, not a viability one.

sections.title: What are the common mistakes?
sections.html:
These are the errors that account for almost every wrong answer people bring to this calculator:

  • Reading against water rather than against fresh medium.
  • Forgetting to multiply by the dilution factor after diluting.
  • Using a cuvette with a different path length without correcting.

sections.title: Calculators that go with this one
sections.html:
This tool answers one step of the question. The neighbouring steps have their own pages:

Bacterial growth curve. Cell density. Specific growth rate from OD readings.

faq.a: About 8 × 10⁸ E. coli per mL, though this varies two-fold between strains and media.

faq.q: Can I use OD600 to measure growth rate?
faq.a: Yes — in the linear range, ln(OD) against time gives the growth rate, which is what the growth curve calculator does.

faq.q: What does the OD600 to Cell Density actually calculate?
faq.a: It returns corrected OD600, cell density and dry cell weight. Each one is derived by the formula on this page, so you can check any figure by hand.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — and if you change an input, every result updates with it.

faq.q: Why is the answer different from the one in my protocol?
faq.a: Nearly always a unit or a rounding difference. This calculator works in the units printed next to each box, keeps full precision internally and only rounds for display, so recomputing from the rounded numbers on screen can differ in the last digit.

faq.q: Can I use it with the numbers straight from a datasheet?
faq.a: Yes. Every box states its unit, and nothing is converted behind your back, so a figure copied from a datasheet, a kit insert or a protocol goes in as printed.
